objective: Help commuters find the quiet carriage.
takeaway: Look for the crescent on the carriage door.
facts separated by |: A crescent on the carriage door identifies the quiet carriage.
independent evidence: Same recognizable door before and after; crescent on it; no behavioral rules.

objective: Make exhausted commuters feel understood during the effort of finding the carriage.
takeaway: Look for the crescent on the carriage door.
facts separated by |: A crescent on the carriage door identifies the quiet carriage.
independent evidence: The traveler’s weariness feels recognized, and the same sign appears on the door; no promise of silence or relief.

objective: Help visitors find the temporary entrance.
takeaway: Use the courtyard entrance today.
facts separated by |: The main entrance is closed today.|Visitors enter through the courtyard.
independent evidence: Clear route from main door to courtyard, no claimed opening time.

objective: Show a beginner how to stand a phone up using two clips and a card.
takeaway: Clips hold opposite bottom corners to make a stand.
facts separated by |: Two identical flat-bottom clamps grip opposite bottom corners of an upright stiff card.
independent evidence: Both clamps visible under opposite corners; show what each grips without implying load certification.

objective: Show the action needed to pass thread through an eye.
takeaway: Push the tip through the eye, then pull it out the far side.
facts separated by |: A needle eye is a small opening.|The thread passes through the opening and comes out on the far side.
independent evidence: Same thread tip and bounded eye, actual passage rather than a label.

objective: Help someone make a centered fold.
takeaway: Match the edges before pressing the crease.
audience: Child who can follow one action
facts separated by |: An unmarked rectangular sheet folds in half when opposite edges meet.
independent evidence: Same sheet bends, matching edges are visible, then crease is pressed.

objective: Help someone open a sleeve without tearing it.
takeaway: Press the sides to widen the mouth.
facts separated by |: The sleeve opens at one end when its two long sides are pressed gently inward.
independent evidence: Mouth visibly widens without a cut or tear; action precedes ending.

objective: Help people choose a cover for wet weather.
takeaway: Compare the water-resistant layer, not the handle color.
facts separated by |: One cover beads water on its surface.|The other lets the same spray through onto paper beneath.
independent evidence: Same spray and paper; moisture contrast visible. No claim of complete waterproofing.

objective: Help a commuter notice that handle color is not evidence of weather protection.
takeaway: Compare the water-resistant layer, not the handle color.
facts separated by |: One cover beads water on its surface.|The other lets the same spray through onto paper beneath.
independent evidence: Opening should show the tempting color cue and redirect it to the water demonstration; same facts as C08.

objective: Encourage someone to label both ends before unplugging.
takeaway: A matched label makes a cord easier to trace.
facts separated by |: Two similar cords cross behind a desk.|Matching marks can identify the ends of one cord.
independent evidence: Show a small avoidable mix-up and its payoff; no lecture or electrical claims.

objective: Make bringing a bottle feel manageable.
takeaway: Put the bottle beside your keys tonight.
audience: Someone who keeps forgetting their bottle
facts separated by |: A bottle can be placed beside keys as a visible reminder.
independent evidence: Show a concrete low-effort action, no invented environmental savings.

objective: Tell a small story about admitting a mistake.
takeaway: The character chooses to ask for help rather than guess.
audience: A child watching on a phone
facts separated by |: Fiction: Mina has a parcel with an unreadable number.|She asks the doorman to confirm the address.
independent evidence: A visible decision and consequence, no invented address treated as fact.

objective: Tell a short story about sharing control.
takeaway: Two friends can take turns rather than tug.
facts separated by |: Fiction: Jo and Pat both want the same spool.|They agree on turns.
independent evidence: One spool and altered action carry the ending; don't have the narrator state the moral twice.

objective: Show the relief of being noticed without a speech.
takeaway: A small gesture can make someone feel welcome.
facts separated by |: Fiction: A traveler enters a busy café.|A friend moves a bag off the adjacent chair.
independent evidence: Story starts at a choice; removal makes the offered seat visually evident.

objective: Help a beginner identify a right angle.
takeaway: A corner is a right angle when it matches a square corner.
facts separated by |: A right angle is 90 degrees.|A square has right-angle corners.
independent evidence: Show the same square corner meeting one angle and missing the other.

objective: Explain counting spaces between marks.
takeaway: The third step above 20 is 23 when each space is one.
facts separated by |: Major ticks show 20 and 25.|Each interval is one degree.
independent evidence: Equal ticks, starting point and three gaps visibly counted.

objective: Help a learner identify one half.
takeaway: Two of four equal parts make one half.
facts separated by |: Four parts are equal.|Two are dark blue.
independent evidence: Same four parts visible throughout.

objective: Explain why a shadow grows nearer the light.
takeaway: The same card can make a larger shadow near the lamp.
facts separated by |: Keep lamp and wall fixed.|Same-size card moves closer to lamp.
independent evidence: Fix the geometry and show actual shadow size contrast.

objective: Help a learner count an elapsed interval.
takeaway: 11:50 to 12:10 is twenty minutes.
facts separated by |: From 11:50 to 12:00 is ten minutes.|From 12:00 to 12:10 is ten minutes.
independent evidence: A shared timeline with two visible ten-minute segments.

objective: Explain accumulation across hours.
takeaway: Second-hour rain can be 3 mm while the running total is 5 mm.
facts separated by |: First hour 2 mm.|Second hour 3 mm.
independent evidence: Show both interval and cumulative displays with unambiguous values.

objective: Teach undo of one attribute.
takeaway: Undoing recolor does not undo the move.
facts separated by |: A blue square moves right.|Then becomes orange.|Undo only the last change.
independent evidence: Show same square and right-hand final position with original blue.

objective: Teach grouping before counting.
takeaway: Three groups of four make twelve.
facts separated by |: Show three equal rows of four counters.
independent evidence: Show exactly twelve objects, separated into three groups.

objective: Show how to open a mock envelope by its tab.
takeaway: Lift the loose tab, not the body.
facts separated by |: A mock envelope has a free flap tab.|Pulling the tab raises the flap.
independent evidence: Show a recognizable tab and visible hinge action.

objective: Show how to bring two sides together to make a cone.
takeaway: Overlap the two edges of a paper sector.
facts separated by |: A sector can be rolled into a cone by bringing its two radial edges together.
independent evidence: Same piece; edges and overlap visibly track.

objective: Help a visitor trace a route on a map.
takeaway: Start at the dot and follow the arrows.
facts separated by |: The route begins at a green dot and follows east then north.
independent evidence: One start, correct turning order.

objective: Show how to separate mock keys.
takeaway: Use the tag, not the key outline.
facts separated by |: Three identical keys have red, blue, and red tags.
independent evidence: Groups put both reds together; no extra key.

objective: Show how to save a page without bending it.
takeaway: Slip the marker between pages and leave its top visible.
facts separated by |: A flat bookmark goes between two pages, leaving its top above the book.
independent evidence: Show same bookmark partially occluded and no bent page.

objective: Show where to tuck a note into a clip.
takeaway: The clip jaws go on the paper edge.
facts separated by |: A spring clip can grip the edge of a note.
independent evidence: Show jaws actually over the note and let go.

objective: Help a visitor find the working elevator.
takeaway: Use the elevator beside the stairs today.
facts separated by |: The lobby elevator is closed today.|The elevator beside the stairs is open.
independent evidence: Show one clear landmark and door. No times or access promises.

objective: Make arrival instructions easy to remember.
takeaway: Check in at the blue table.
facts separated by |: The blue table is the check-in point.|It is inside the main room.
independent evidence: Show the correct table inside; no invented requirements.

objective: Prompt people to take the scheduled break.
takeaway: The session resumes at two fifteen.
facts separated by |: The next workshop segment begins at 2:15.
independent evidence: Read exactly 2:15; do not invent duration.

objective: Help residents identify the returns box.
takeaway: Use the box marked with a triangle.
facts separated by |: A triangle marks the returns box at the entrance.
independent evidence: Readable triangle on the box, not a floating icon.

objective: Help participants go to the right room.
takeaway: Meet in room 12 instead of room 8.
facts separated by |: Today the group meets in room 12.|Room 8 is the original room.
independent evidence: Distinguish old and new room numbers on clear doors.

objective: Help an attendee get to the issue desk.
takeaway: The ticket desk is past the stairs.
facts separated by |: The ticket desk is beyond the stairs along the corridor.
independent evidence: Correct order from stairs to desk with no speculative ticket price.

objective: Help residents recognize the bike room.
takeaway: The wheel symbol marks the bike room door.
facts separated by |: The door with the wheel symbol is the bike room.
independent evidence: Symbol unmistakably on the intended door.

objective: Teach the difference between fill and capacity.
takeaway: Same cups can hold different amounts now without having different capacities.
facts separated by |: Both cups are identical.|One has more water now.
independent evidence: Identical outline and different visible water levels; no invented volume.

objective: Help someone choose a cable that reaches.
takeaway: Compare the usable length from the same start.
facts separated by |: One cord is 1 m.|The other is 2 m.|The gap to reach is 1.5 m.
independent evidence: Same scale and origin; only long cord reaches.

objective: Help a small-screen viewer tell which label reads faster.
takeaway: A short label with contrast is easier to find here.
facts separated by |: One dark label reads TEA on a pale lid.|The alternative is pale text on a pale lid.
independent evidence: Show both lids at the same size; don't generalize to legal accessibility certification.

objective: Help someone choose a quicker route in this example.
takeaway: A longer walk can finish first if the shorter route waits.
facts separated by |: Route A walks 4 minutes and waits 5.|Route B walks 6 minutes without waiting.
independent evidence: Common start; 9 versus 6, wait distinguishable.

objective: Prevent equating height with volume.
takeaway: Height alone doesn't tell which vessel holds more.
facts separated by |: Two differently shaped clear vessels each contain the same 100 ml.
independent evidence: Identical measured pours or clear graduated evidence, no visual implication of equal heights.

objective: Help choose a cloth wide enough.
takeaway: The cloth must span the width, not just the length.
facts separated by |: The cloth is 90 by 120 cm.|Table A is 80 by 100 cm.|Table B is 95 by 100 cm.
independent evidence: Same cloth compared onto two outlines with overflow/shortfall correct.

objective: Encourage copying the contact before losing a note.
takeaway: Keep a second copy where you will find it.
facts separated by |: A paper contact note can be misplaced.|A second copy can be kept in a chosen spot.
independent evidence: Show a practical choice and consequence; use no real contact data.

objective: Encourage someone to move a bag out of a walkway.
takeaway: Put it beside the bench, out of the walking line.
facts separated by |: Fictional scene: a bag sits in a public walkway.|Space is available beside the bench.
independent evidence: Before blocks the route; after frees it. No safety statistics.

objective: Encourage checking a label before choosing.
takeaway: Look for the unit price first.
facts separated by |: A unit price states the cost for one unit.
independent evidence: One action demonstrated; no invented savings.

objective: Invite a tired viewer to take a short break.
takeaway: It's okay to pause before the next task.
facts separated by |: Use fictional illustration only.
independent evidence: Recognizable tension and small pause, no medical benefit or guilt.

objective: Encourage returning a tool to its place.
takeaway: A visible home makes the tool easier to find later.
facts separated by |: An empty labeled tool hook shows where a missing tool goes.
independent evidence: Show hook and return; give payoff rather than blame.

objective: Lower the barrier to asking for directions.
takeaway: One clear question is enough to start.
facts separated by |: Fiction: a visitor is unsure which corridor to take.
independent evidence: No promised response; an approachable exchange and a single question.

objective: Tell a story through one choice.
takeaway: Splitting the last orange lets both friends share.
facts separated by |: Fiction: two friends find one orange and decide to split it.
independent evidence: One orange becomes two pieces, no unexplained replacement.

objective: Tell a visual joke about an almost-mistake.
takeaway: A forgotten object can turn an exit into a return.
facts separated by |: Fiction: Ren notices rain at the door, returns for an umbrella, then leaves.
independent evidence: Clear reason for turn; same umbrella outside.

objective: Tell a story about following through.
takeaway: The character returns what they borrowed.
facts separated by |: Fiction: Sana borrows a green book and later returns that same book.
independent evidence: Recognizable book and distinct change of possession.

objective: Tell a small story about noticing.
takeaway: Recognizing a tiny detail helps reunite a pair.
facts separated by |: Fiction: Emi finds a glove with a triangle patch.|Its partner has the same patch.
independent evidence: Matching detail, same gloves; visual payoff.

objective: Tell a short story with a visible payoff.
takeaway: Fixing one small detail can let an object work again.
facts separated by |: Fiction: a loose strap button comes off; the character reattaches it.
independent evidence: Show the same strap and reattached button, no how-to repair claim.

objective: Tell a story about someone making a clue visible.
takeaway: The character turns the sign to help the next person.
facts separated by |: Fiction: a wayfinding sign faces a wall; Ada turns it toward the path.
independent evidence: Real orientation change and legible clue, not merely a narrator claim.

topic: Two people at a narrow crossing
objective: Tell a short story about waiting your turn.
takeaway: One person steps aside and both get across.
facts separated by |: Fiction: two travelers meet at a narrow footbridge; one waits until the other crosses.
independent evidence: Show a meaningful choice and positions in order.
